adjudication_label: batch_2:TEM characterization methods and resolution limits for defect imaging
canonical_question: Why were two different TEM systems (Tecnai F30 and Titan 80-300) used for post-characterization, and is there a difference in resolution or contrast for the specific defects sought?

question_variants.question: Why were two different TEM systems (Tecnai F30 and Titan 80-300) used for post-characterization, and is there a difference in resolution or contrast for the specific defects sought?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence confirms two TEM systems were used (FEI Tecnai F30 and FEI Titan 80-300), both operating at 300 keV. However, the provided text does not contain information regarding the specific resolution differences between these systems or the contrast mechanisms for the specific defects sought, nor does it explain the rationale for using two distinct systems.

answers.answer: The post-characterization was performed using two TEM systems: FEI Tecnai F30 and FEI Titan 80-300, both operating at 300 keV. The document does not provide a comparison of their resolution capabilities or contrast differences for the specific defects.
answers.measurement_outcome: Two systems listed: Tecnai F30 and Titan 80-300
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative resolution data provided in text
evidence_spans: A detailed characterization of the morphology and phase details of the as-deposited HEA films results in a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm) with an underlying single-phase BCC, with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.
